done.what: Pieces carry traced `parts`: the fig's pot (soil left out), both artworks' frame rings (outer outline minus the canvas), the TV's frame and stand (screen left out), the bedroom lamp's and the new floor lamp's shade and base. Finish rows name their part (Planter → pot, Frame → frame, a TV's Finish → body); `finishRowFor(piece)` offers a part row only where the part is traced; `customizePart` sends the finish and its colour to that part (a lamp: shade for a shade/glass finish, base for a metal) and the engine paints only it — or refuses when a row names a part the photo doesn't mark. render-test: fig pot |Δ| 49.7 with leaves |Δ| 0.0; TV screen |Δ| 0.0.

Remove, piece by piece, redone and looked at. Sofa: the armchair's hidden side comes back mirrored from its own visible side (`mend: 'mirror'`, axis), its hidden front leg too; the rug goes on under the sofa with its own weave, laid from a clean patch on the rug's own light (`mend: 'texture'`, no chevrons, no straight seam); the coffee table stands over its own shade (`mend: 'shade'`) with its hidden front edge mended along its rows; the sofa arm's shadow on the rug goes with it; the throw's top retraced. Console: the TV's two feet go with it (`restsOn`) and the TV hangs on the wall; the plate takes the pampas' soft edge (no smudge). Coffee table: the console's bottom rail is continued along its slope (`rails`, alongFill) — no stair steps; the bowl's rim goes with it. Armchair: the floor lamp is its own piece now and stays standing, its pole continued behind the chair. Fig: the plate takes its shadow (no pale blotches). Every mend lays over the picture as it was before the plate went on (no half-plate ghosts at a mend's soft edge), and never over a piece standing in front.

Sofa Remove + armchair Replace: the chair is whole (its mended side takes the Replace's colour too — `paintMask` joins what was mended of a piece), the coffee table's front is no longer sliced, the rug's left edge continues instead of a straight seam.

Coffee table: its bowl, books, cup and candle are cut out by their own outlines (no padded island), the lit and shaded top seeded, its front edge included — one tone. Right sheer curtain is painted as its whole traced outline (`whole`: shaded folds by the wall, no torn edge); the left curtain's header is in its cut. The rug is its whole outline (no beige rims), running on under the sofa.

The floor's sofa cutout follows the sofa's real top edge and the armchair's feet (the strip between the sofa back and the skirting is painted); the sofa's left edge and leg cutout tightened — no white halo on walnut. The demo's pre-rendered edit and its golden-hour relight re-rendered with the final engine (scripts/viz/demo-renders.mts; swatches still in step).

Kitchen worktops: the back run's front edge and the island's back edge traced from the photo — Granite Black no longer steps down the drawer fronts by the hob, no white fleck at the island's corner. Bedroom back wall reaches the wardrobe's diagonal top; the wedge between the left nightstand and the bed is seeded and the nightstand's side face cut out; the headboard cutout's left edge follows the duvet; the glasses on the nightstand are glass (`glass`: the paint shows through, their glints stay).

See-through things in front of a surface are `soft` outlines, keyed pixel by pixel against the wall's own colour around (shade-tolerant, edge pixels unmixed): the pampas plumes, the gap under the armchair's arm, the fig's leaves — navy fills between the fronds with no blocky silhouette; the vase, its handle side and the cup are cut exactly (no white box on the console top); the pot rim is clean.

Kitchen floor: the stools' legs and footrest rails are keyed out of the floor (soft outlines over the stools' bases, darker-in-shade counting little, hue counting fully) — herringbone runs between the rails, the legs keep their walnut.
A drawn surface behind a see-through piece (the fig) takes the piece's outline out and keys the wall back between its leaves — no octagon of unpainted wall.

Each traced plane lays a pattern in its own perspective by containment (the band under the dropped ceiling is in phase, no stray block by the tall unit; slivers take their neighbour's); a wallpaper stops at the kitchen window's reveals (`reveals`: paint covers them, paper doesn't — no hairlines, no stepped joins).
The living room ceiling cuts out its round diffuser and four downlights — a wallpaper or a paint leaves the fixtures as they are.

referencePalette reads with room to spare (k+3 clusters, merged back where two are one colour, ΔE<9), so walnut and sage stay apart at every size the editor keeps a reference at (512–1600 px tested): floor #8A6F54 (≈ #8B6F55), walls #DEDAD3, joinery #2F3C45. Browser and Node use the same function with the same k.
